title: Yosi Maoni
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin, end of chapter 2, it is told that he once preached in the synagogue at Tiberias. (In Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 81, he preached in the synagogue of Maon; Hyman treats the accounts as referring to the same place, since Maon was near Tiberias, as explained in Sotah 1:8.) “Hear, O priests”—why do you not toil in Torah? [Etc.] “Did I not give you twenty-four gifts?” They answered, “They give us nothing.” “The king takes everything”—“for yours is the judgment”: “I said this to you.” He meant the house of the patriarchs. Rabbi Yudan the Nasi (the second) heard and became angry; Yosi was afraid and fled. Rabbi Yochanan and Resh Lakish went up to appease the Nasi, saying that Yosi was a great man. He asked, “Can he answer everything I ask him?” They said yes. He asked Yosi what “for their mother has played the harlot” meant: “Was our mother Sarah a harlot?” Yosi replied, “Like daughter, like mother; like mother, like daughter; like the generation, like the Nasi; like the Nasi, like the generation.” This Yerushalmi is cited in Rabbenu Chananel’s commentary on Sanhedrin 22a, where the name is Rabbi Yosef Maoni. Hyman says the author of Mavo HaYerushalmi erred on this point.

notes.text: The named Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin2:6 paragraph supports the preaching and dialogue. Hyman’s Bereshit Rabbah chapter81 locator is retained; the older supplied digital parallel was numbered80:1.

The inspected Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:6 directly contains Yosi Maoni’s preaching, Yudan Nasi’s response and the dialogue mediated by Yochanan and Resh Lakish. Hyman’s Maon/Tiberias comparison, Yudan II identification, Yosef spelling in Rabbenu Chananel and criticism of Mavo HaYerushalmi remain his account; the supplied Bereshit Rabbah 81 versus earlier digital 80:1 difference is not silently normalized.
